title: Capacity oscillation mitigation and scaling cadence for Dedicated pools
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: Several customers (mid-market and enterprise) have reported oscillating Dedicated pool scale decisions over short windows. Autoscalers repeatedly add and remove capacity as transient spikes arrive, which increases cost and causes cold-start latency for downstream requests. This ticket coordinates a cross-functional initiative to reduce oscillation, stabilize scaling cadence, and provide an ops playbook for graceful degradation and cost corridors.

Objectives: 1) Reduce unnecessary scale-up/scale-down events by 40% for targeted workloads. 2) Preserve 99th percentile latency SLOs for high-priority pools during smoothing periods. 3) Provide a documented cadence (policy + telemetry) for thresholds, hysteresis, and predictive warm-pool behavior.

Approach: - Define a configurable smoothing window + derivative-based trigger to differentiate sustained demand from spikes. - Introduce a cost-corridor guardrail: short-term excess scale allowed only up to budget threshold, otherwise route to fallback models/regions. - Pilot predictive warm pools for customers with recurring daily peaks. - Add autoscale circuit-breaker: if scale rate > X events / 10m, flip to conservative mode and notify oncall. - Instrument new telemetry (scale_event_id, decision_reason, predicted_trajectory) to surface in Console and alerts.

Scope: MVP focuses on Dedicated reserved pools and the autoscale controller; Hosted runtime fallbacks and Private deployments are out of scope for MVP but will be included in follow-ups.
milestones: Week 1: Design and decision meeting; finalize smoothing algorithm and cost-corridor concept
Week 2: Prototype controller changes + local simulation harness
Week 3: Integrate telemetry and Console visualization (per-pool scale event timeline)
Week 4: Canary in a single customer environment (non-critical) + measure oscillation delta
Week 5: Expand to two more customers, tune thresholds, publish runbook
Release: console-2026.03 includes UI controls and opt-in toggle for predictive warm pools
acceptance_criteria: Autoscale events per hour reduced by >= 40% on pilot pools compared to baseline (measured over 7d)
P99 request latency for prioritized pools does not regress more than 5% during smoothing window
Console shows per-pool scale event timeline with decision_reason and predicted_trajectory
Runbook published with step-by-step recovery and recommended thresholds; ops runbook reviewed by SRE
Opt-in toggle and billing guardrail implemented; product tests covering rollback behavior exist
